distinguishing_features: Surface-energy modification via a lubricant-infused porous (SLIPS) coating on the heat-transfer wall, rather than a procedural duty-cycle change or a monitoring inference
Replacement of the solid-liquid fouling interface with a lubricating liquid-liquid interface to lower effective adhesion below operating wall shear
Continuous self-cleaning during production without shutdowns, relying on existing process shear to shed deposit
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce protein deposit adhesion on the hot heat-transfer surface so fouling layers do not accumulate and raise energy demand during pasteurization.
parsed.viable_reason: As written the SLIPS layer is not physically sound at the stated scale: the 100 cSt PDMS lubricant would be sheared and depleted by 2.7 Pa wall shear at 1.5 m/s over a 72-hour dairy run, food-grade lubricant retention/leak containment is unproven, and the claimed adhesion reduction to <1 Pa is asserted without support.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art applies a lubricant-infused porous surface-energy modification to a heat-transfer wall; the interface-replacement mechanism is not a routine parameter tweak of the cited approaches.
